summary: NFL 4-closure certification sweep on live backend. 5 of 7 verification items pass; 1 CRITICAL failure (alt-ladder display parity) and 1 real pytest failure. Pytest overall: 27 passed / 4 failed (1 real product behavior, 3 test-scaffolding motor/asyncio loop bugs). Auth OK (demo@lockscore.ai/demo123), /api/picks/today?sport=NFL&lite=true returns 200 with 908 NFL picks and valid per-pick pick_date=2026-09-11, ATD leaderboard reachable with V2 engine provenance, nfl_player_weekly deferred ingest hydrated (129,808 docs, seasons 2019-2026), Lock Score cap correctly removed (108 picks with edge_percent<=0 still carry LS>90). CRITICAL: 801/801 NFL alt-lock picks emitted from /api/picks/today still show raw provider label 'Over N.5 Player X · ALT LOCK' instead of required 'N+ [Market]' format — _prop_market_label unit tests pass in isolation (14/14) but the wiring from publisher → pick.market field is not calling it (or is_alt flag not propagating). Star-player canonical name check inconclusive (A.J. Brown / JSN not in today's live slate). NO CODE CHANGES MADE per directive.

critical.issue: Alt-ladder display truth NOT applied end-to-end. All 801 NFL alt-lock picks carry raw label 'Over N.5 Player X Yds  · ALT LOCK' instead of the required 'N+ [Market]' milestone form (e.g. 'Cade Otton Over 14.5 Player Reception Yds  · ALT LOCK' should be '15+ Receiving Yards'). _prop_market_label unit tests all pass (14/14), so the formatter is correct — but the publish pipeline is not invoking it (or is_alt/side flags not set) when writing pick.market. Verified via scripts/nfl_alt_ladder_truth_probe.py which shows every published alt-line row with alt=False and raw label. Reference: backend/sports_engine.py:5704 (_prop_market_label) — confirm callers pass sport='NFL', side='over', point=<line>, market_key ending in '_alternate'.

Only 1/67 trap-chalk alts carry the 4 required flags (alt_edge_cap_applied + apex_status=NOT_APEX + apex_lock=False + correct apex_reason). Sample failing pick: 'Christian McCaffrey Over 24.5 Player Rush Yds  · ALT LOCK' edge=0.0 pre_elite=98.9 lock_score=97.9 apex=NOT_APEX cap_reason=nfl_alt_edge_not_positive:0.00pct_no_elite_authority. NOTE: This test appears STALE relative to closure #3 (Lock Score edge_percent<=0 cap removal). LS=97.9 on edge=0.0 is consistent with the new closure (cap removed), so the assertion 'alt_edge_cap_applied=True' now conflicts with the current design. Main-agent decision needed: either the test contract needs updating, or the closure inadvertently disabled the flag emission on trap-chalk rows.

minor.issue: 3 tests fail with 'RuntimeError: got Future attached to a different loop' — motor async cursor iterated inside a fresh event loop while the AsyncIOMotorClient was bound to a different loop. Not a product bug — test-scaffolding bug. Tests: test_trap_chalk_all_have_nonpositive_edge_and_capped_lock_score, test_positive_edge_nfl_alts_have_no_cap_flag, test_nfl_alt_ladder_monotone_and_odds_present. Fix pattern: build the AsyncIOMotorClient inside the same loop that runs run_until_complete (or use pytest-asyncio fixtures).

Both hard-crash at import-time on KeyError: 'EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL' because they use os.environ[...] with no fallback. Backend .env is populated but the pytest process env is not seeded. Suggest either load_dotenv('/app/frontend/.env') or fall back to a local http://localhost:8001. Manual workaround used in this run: export EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL before pytest.

Inconsistent version tags: v2_engine_version='1.0.0' AND model_version='legacy_unknown' on same document. atd_evidence.source='nfl_atd_engine' confirms V2 is producing the pick, but the legacy model_version label survives from an earlier writer path. Not a functional failure — provenance still tracks V2 — but the mixed tag is confusing for downstream analytics.

rca_of_issue: PRIMARY BUG — Alt-ladder display parity: _prop_market_label (sports_engine.py:5704-5782) is correctly implemented and 14/14 unit tests pass, but production /api/picks/today?sport=NFL&lite=true returns 801/801 alt-lock picks with pick.market = raw provider string ('Over N.5 Player X Yds · ALT LOCK'). Two candidate root causes: (a) the publisher composing pick.market is bypassing _prop_market_label for player-prop alts (a separate code path from the goalscorer/first_td players formatter around line 7502), or (b) the market_key seen by the formatter does not end with '_alternate' at publish time (the probe shows `alt=False` on the emitted row), so the guard `if is_alt` never triggers. RECOMMENDED PROBE: grep sports_engine.py for the exact writer of pick.market on the lite path and log the market_key + is_alt at that call. This is a wiring/plumbing gap, not a formatter defect — DO NOT modify _prop_market_label itself. SECONDARY — TrapChalk flag test failure: LS cap removal closure (#3) was applied but the alt_edge_cap_applied flag emission (test_iter137 requirement) may have been dropped as a side-effect. Confirm intent with prior main-agent before code changes.
